MIGRATION: db/schema.ts changes ran through `npm run db:generate` cleanly and produced exactly ONE new migration, db/migrations/0033_sad_human_torch.sql (2 ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statements on learners: first_name, last_name, dob, user_id + 1 ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN is_active on household_members + 1 ADD CONSTRAINT FK learners.user_id -> users.id). This is a single nullable FK — the CLAUDE.md composite-FK-ordering caveat does not apply (verified: no composite UNIQUE+FK combination in this migration, plain ADD COLUMN + single FK only, correctly ordered by drizzle-kit already).

FAILURE — db:migrate cannot complete in this sandbox (root-caused, not just a timeout guess): `npm run db:migrate` was run in the background and produced ZERO output after 13+ minutes (task bxtn691tq, manually stopped). Diagnosed with three independent, more targeted probes against the exact DATABASE_URL host (dpg-d8jegg3bc2fs73bkhqm0-a.virginia-postgres.render.com, the DEV db, confirmed NOT prod): (1) raw TCP connect — succeeds instantly. (2) postgres.js driver `select 1` query with connect_timeout:10 — hangs past 15s with no error/data. (3) hand-rolled Postgres wire-protocol probe: TCP connects, SSLRequest is sent and the server replies 'S' (accept) immediately, the subsequent TLS handshake over that socket completes successfully (TLSv1.3) — but after sending the Postgres StartupMessage (protocol 3.0, user=sacad_user, database=sacad) over the now-TLS-wrapped socket, the server NEVER responds (15s timeout, zero bytes back). This precisely refines and confirms the exact same limitation phase-0's notes already documented for `npm run build`'s /(shell)/about static generation ('TCP connects... but the Postgres protocol handshake hangs indefinitely') — this sandbox's network path can complete a TCP+TLS handshake to this Postgres host but the server-side (or an intermediate proxy) never completes the Postgres application-level startup exchange. This is an environment/network limitation, NOT a defect in the generated migration SQL or schema, and is outside the phase's file scope to fix. INVARIANT CHECK COULD NOT BE PERFORMED: db:migrate did not apply (blocked before it could even authenticate), so 'applies with no gap in the migration sequence' cannot be confirmed, and a post-migrate db:generate producing zero new migrations likewise cannot be confirmed against a live DB.

FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT: no code changes are needed to retry — only re-run `npm run db:migrate` (and then the invariant re-check: `npm run db:generate` must show no new migration) from an environment where this Postgres host is actually reachable at the application layer, then run `npm test` full suite + attempt `npm run build` (expected to hit the same known /(shell)/about failure per prior phases, non-blocking), then commit. All schema/repository/route/test code in this write-up is believed complete and correct pending that live verification — do not redo the implementation from scratch.

phases.title: G2 — Single active-year course visibility across Settings/Gradebook/Learning-time; rollover hides-but-keeps prior-year copies
G7a — Editable start/end time for scheduled classes

outputs.notes: No code changed; investigation only, per the plan's explicit instruction to read the schedule feature first since it was uncertain whether start/end time fields already exist read-only or are entirely absent. FINDING: they are entirely absent as persisted data — this phase requires a schema change and is therefore out of the declared fileScope. Details: features/schedule/types.ts's ScheduleBlock/LessonScheduleEntry.startTime/endTime are NOT stored anywhere; they are synthesized fresh on every render by buildDailySchedule() in features/schedule/server/service.ts, which walks the day's LessonTask list and assigns each one a start time by adding parseDurationMinutes(lesson.estimatedDuration, defaultDurationMinutes) to a running cursor that begins at a fixed ScheduleSettings.startTime ('08:30' hardcoded in features/schedule/front/pages/SchedulePage.tsx) with a transitionMinutes gap between blocks. lesson.estimatedDuration (features/plan/types.ts LessonDuration) is a bucket enum ('15min'|'30min'|'45min'|'1hr'|'custom'), not a clock time. The db/schema.ts lesson_tasks table (line 261-283) has no clock-time columns whatsoever — only estimatedDuration (text bucket), plannedStartDate/dueDate (dates, not times); there is no separate schedule-block/schedule-override table anywhere in db/schema.ts. The timeline's 'Edit lesson' pencil icon (features/schedule/front/components/ScheduleTimeline.tsx) navigates to /lessons?editId=... (the planner's LessonTaskForm) which also has no time fields to edit, consistent with there being nothing persisted to edit. CONCLUSION: making start/end time editable-and-persisted (per the testsFirst requirement: 'changing start/end time and saving persists the new times and they are shown after reload') requires adding time columns (e.g. to lesson_tasks, or a new table) plus a Drizzle migration. This phase's fileScope is only app/(shell)/plan/schedule/page.tsx and features/schedule/ — it explicitly does NOT include db/schema.ts or db/migrations/, and the orchestrator's spawn instructions explicitly said to stop and fail rather than attempt a migration if this were found. Stopping here per that instruction. FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT: this phase needs to be re-scoped (fileScope must add db/schema.ts, db/migrations/, and likely features/plan/types.ts + features/plan/server/repository.ts for the LessonTask persistence layer) before it can be implemented; a migration will also need the live-DB invariant check that phase-g3 already found blocked in this sandbox (Postgres wire-protocol StartupMessage never gets a response from the dev DB host), so this migration should be planned as a 'strong'-tier, gated phase like G3.
outputs.notesForModelTier: standard tier was sufficient to identify the scope gap; the actual fix belongs in a strong-tier gated phase per the reasoning above.

This phase's fileScope (app/(shell)/plan/schedule/page.tsx, features/schedule/) excludes db/schema.ts and db/migrations/, and the spawn instructions explicitly directed failing the phase rather than widening scope into a migration. Needs re-planning as a schema-touching phase before implementation.
